text.title: rust-tokio-async Core Rules
text.summary: 12 testable rules grounding the rust-tokio-async methodology. Each rule pairs a binary check with a sourced rationale.

rule.statement: Classify the workload (fixed-small / CPU-heavy / large-bounded / dynamic) before writing code. Pick the matching primitive.
rule.rationale: Wrong primitive either over-engineers small N or OOM-risks large N.

rule.statement: Use tokio::try_join! for fixed N <= 20 futures collected together, short-circuiting on the first error.
rule.rationale: try_join! resolves all futures simultaneously; large N overloads pools.

rule.statement: Wrap CPU-heavy work (Argon2, bcrypt, regex compile, image, zip) in tokio::task::spawn_blocking; await with .await?? to propagate both join error and inner Result. The same applies to any blocking syscall on an async path: `std::fs`, `std::thread::sleep`, a blocking sync mutex, or any CPU loop over ~1ms.
rule.rationale: CPU futures starve the executor thread, blocking every other task scheduled on it. A blocking call is indistinguishable from a slow one to the scheduler — it simply freezes the worker until it returns; `spawn_blocking` (or `tokio::fs`) moves it onto the dedicated blocking pool.

rule.statement: Process large collections with futures::stream::buffer_unordered(N) + tokio::sync::Semaphore::acquire_owned for explicit concurrency control.
rule.rationale: Semaphore adds an explicit capacity token visible to logging/metrics.

rule.statement: Use tokio::task::JoinSet instead of Vec<JoinHandle<T>>. JoinSet cancels remaining tasks on drop, preventing leaks. A bare `tokio::spawn(...)` whose JoinHandle is dropped is FORBIDDEN.
rule.rationale: Vec<JoinHandle> requires explicit abort() loops; forgetting them leaves tasks running. A dropped handle is worse still — the task leaks AND its panic is swallowed, so the failure never reaches a log. JoinSet propagates the panic through the `Result` returned by `join_next`.

rule.statement: Wrap every external I/O call in tokio::time::timeout — no safe default for a missing timeout.
rule.rationale: A hung external call exhausts Tokio worker threads.

rule.statement: In tokio::select! with non-cancellation-safe futures, document each branch's cancel-safety with a comment.
rule.rationale: select! drops the losing future at the next .await, silently losing partial state.

rule.statement: Never hold std::sync::MutexGuard across .await. Prefer mpsc, or use tokio::sync::Mutex when async-aware locks are required.
rule.rationale: std::sync::MutexGuard is !Send; holding it across .await compile-errors or deadlocks.

rule.statement: Cargo features MUST declare the runtime flavour explicitly (`tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", ...] }`) and the runtime build MUST set `worker_threads`. A default-runtime build in production is FORBIDDEN.
rule.rationale: The default `multi_thread` flavour picks worker_count = CPU cores, which is frequently wrong for the workload (and wrong twice over inside a cgroup-limited container). Writing the number down surfaces the decision and makes it reviewable.

rule.statement: `mpsc::channel(capacity)` MUST use a bounded capacity sized to the measured load. `mpsc::unbounded_channel` is FORBIDDEN on a production path.
rule.rationale: An unbounded channel accumulates without limit whenever the consumer is slower than the producer, and the failure mode is an overnight OOMKill rather than a visible slowdown. A bounded channel back-pressures the producer instead. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: The service MUST listen for `ctrl_c` (or a signal stream) and propagate cancellation through a `CancellationToken` or a shutdown channel. An abrupt drop with no cleanup is FORBIDDEN.
rule.rationale: Without coordinated shutdown, in-flight requests are dropped mid-write: clients see TCP resets and partially written bodies, and a rolling deploy turns into an error spike.

rule.statement: Skip when the input does not satisfy the Applies-If preconditions or another methodology owns this output shape.
rule.rationale: Prevents duplicate work and wrong-tool application.
